question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{99+6x}$ at the point where $x=-3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=99+6x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (6) \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{99+6x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-3} & ={(\frac{3}{\sqrt{99+6x}})|}_{x=-3} \\  & =\frac{6}{2\sqrt{99+6(-3)}} \\  & =\frac{6}{2\sqrt{81}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(x)=\sqrt{-6x+82}.$ We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-6x+82.$ Then $f=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-6) \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{u}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{\sqrt{-6x+82}}.\end{aligned}

$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{3x+61}-3{x}^{3}$ at the point where $x=-4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Let $f(x)=\sqrt{3x+61}.$ We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=3x+61.$ Then $f=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (3) \\  & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{u}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3x+61}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3x+61}}-9x^{2}.
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-4} & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3(-4)+61}}-9(-4)^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{14}-144 \\  & =-\frac{2013}{14}.\end{aligned}
$$
